sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: AS A MORE PROMINENT...ELONGATED MID-LEVEL CIRCULATION CONTINUES TO PIVOT IN A GENERAL WESTERLY DIRECTION ACROSS NORTHEASTERN CANADA...MODELS INDICATE THAT THE CLOSED LOW NEAR JAMES BAY WILL DIG ACROSS SOUTHERN QUEBEC BEFORE TURNING EASTWARD TOWARD THE GULF OF ST. LAWRENCE/CANADIAN MARITIMES LATER TODAY/TONIGHT. AS THIS OCCURS...BROAD UPPER TROUGHING TO ITS SOUTH WILL LIKELY SHIFT FROM THE GREAT LAKES REGION THROUGH THE NORTHEASTERN STATES. AT THE SAME TIME...ANOTHER SIGNIFICANT AND PROGRESSIVE IMPULSE WITHIN A LINGERING BELT OF STRONGER WESTERLIES NEAR THE CANADIAN/U.S. BORDER APPEARS LIKELY TO SUPPRESS UPPER RIDGING ACROSS THE NORTHERN PLAINS/UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY...AS YET ANOTHER IMPULSE DIGS ACROSS BRITISH COLUMBIA AND PARTS OF THE PACIFIC NORTHWEST. MEANWHILE...A SUBTROPICAL HIGH CENTER IS EXPECTED TO REMAIN STRONG ACROSS THE FOUR CORNERS STATES. ASSOCIATED WITH THE EVOLVING UPPER PATTERN...A CONTINUED INFLUX OF MOISTURE FROM THE LOWER LATITUDE EASTERN PACIFIC INTO THE SOUTHERN PLATEAU/GREAT BASIN AND ROCKIES WILL SUPPORT CONSIDERABLE THUNDERSTORM ACTIVITY TODAY. WEAK INHIBITION AND SEASONABLY HIGH MOISTURE CONTENT WILL ALSO LIKELY SUPPORT WIDESPREAD CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT A

sections.title: NORTHERN PLAINS INTO THE UPPER MISSISSIPPI VALLEY
sections.text: MODELS INDICATE THAT VERY STEEP LAPSE RATES...ASSOCIATED WITH WARM ELEVATED MIXED LAYER AIR ADVECTING NORTHEAST OF THE CENTRAL ROCKIES...WILL OVERSPREAD THE REGION TODAY...AHEAD OF THE APPROACHING SHORT WAVE IMPULSE. COUPLED WITH INCREASING MOISTURE ON MODEST SOUTHERLY LOW-LEVEL FLOW...CAPE APPEARS LIKELY TO BECOME QUITE LARGE...ON THE ORDER OF 3000-4000 J/KG...THIS AFTERNOON IN THE WARM SECTOR OF A SURFACE LOW/FRONTAL WAVE ACCOMPANYING THE UPPER SYSTEM. AS FAVORABLE LARGE-SCALE FORCING FOR UPWARD VERTICAL CONTRIBUTES TO WEAKENING INHIBITION...THE DEVELOPMENT OF STORMS IS EXPECTED ACROSS THE EASTERN DAKOTAS/WESTERN MINNESOTA BY LATE AFTERNOON. INITIALLY DISCRETE...AND IN THE PRESENCE OF STRONG DEEP LAYER SHEAR BENEATH 35-50 KT WEST NORTHWESTERLY 500 MB FLOW...A FEW SUPERCELLS APPEAR LIKELY...WITH POTENTIAL FOR VERY LARGE HAIL/LOCALIZED STRONG DOWNBURSTS...AND A FEW TORNADOES. sections.title: OHIO VALLEY/CENTRAL APPALACHIANS
sections.text: MODELS ARE SUGGESTIVE THAT AN AREA OF ENHANCED MID-LEVEL FORCING FOR UPWARD VERTICAL MOTION WITHIN THE BROADER SCALE CYCLONIC FLOW WILL OVERSPREAD THE MID/UPPER OHIO VALLEY REGION INTO THE CENTRAL APPALACHIANS THIS AFTERNOON...COINCIDENT WITH MODERATELY STRONG BOUNDARY LAYER DESTABILIZATION DURING THE PEAK HEATING HOURS. FLOW FIELDS AND SHEAR MAY REMAIN FAIRLY MODEST...BUT THE ENVIRONMENT MAY BECOME SUPPORTIVE OF A RELATIVE CONCENTRATION OF STRONG/SEVERE STORMS CAPABLE OF PRODUCING LOCALLY DAMAGING WIND GUSTS.

sections.title: SOUTHEASTERN ARIZONA
sections.text: WIND FIELDS...THOUGH WEAK...APPEAR LIKELY TO BE FAVORABLE FOR STORM PROPAGATION OFF THE HIGHER TERRAIN INTO THE LOWER DESERTS LATE THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING...WHERE A DEEPLY MIXED BOUNDARY LAYER SHOULD BE SUPPORTIVE OF LOCALLY STRONG SURFACE GUSTS ..KERR/STOPPKOTTE.. 07/17/2010

sections.title: NRN PLAINS/UPPER MS VALLEY THIS AFTERNOON INTO TONIGHT
sections.text: A MIDLEVEL SHORTWAVE TROUGH OVER NRN MT AND THE ADJACENT PRAIRIE PROVINCES WILL PROGRESS EWD OVER ND THIS AFTERNOON IN A LARGELY ZONAL FLOW REGIME...AND ESEWD OVER MN/WI TONIGHT. A WEAK SURFACE LOW AND TROUGH/COLD FRONT WILL MOVE EWD WITH THE MIDLEVEL WAVE...WHILE BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS IN THE LOW 70S ACROSS SERN NEB/SRN IA SPREAD NWD TO THE ERN DAKOTAS AND MN BY LATE AFTERNOON. THE MOISTENING WILL COINCIDE WITH DAYTIME HEATING AND WILL OCCUR BENEATH A PLUME OF MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES OF 7.5-8.5 C/KM...WITH THE NET RESULT BEING STRONG INSTABILITY IN THE WARM SECTOR THIS AFTERNOON /MLCAPE 3500-4500 J PER KG/. SEVERE THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT IS EXPECTED BY EARLY-MID AFTERNOON ACROSS ERN ND...NE SD...AND WRN MN AS THE BAND OF MIDLEVEL ASCENT NOW OVER ERN MT/WRN ND COMBINES WITH LOW-LEVEL ASCENT ALONG THE SURFACE TROUGH/FRONT TO REMOVE CONVECTIVE INHIBITION. THE STRONG INSTABILITY WILL SUPPORT RAPID THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT...WHILE FORECAST HODOGRAPHS WITH SOME LOW-LEVEL CURVATURE AND STRONG DEEP-LAYER SHEAR WILL FAVOR SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF PRODUCING VERY LARGE HAIL AND A FEW TORNADOES WITH THE INITIAL DEVELOPMENT. STORM MERGERS/INTERACTIONS SHOULD LEAD TO UPSCALE GROWTH INTO ONE OR MOR

sections.title: WV/VA/NC TODAY
sections.text: AN ONGOING SMALL MCS ACROSS CENTRAL WV APPEARS TO BE ASSOCIATED WITH A SUBTLE EMBEDDED MID-UPPER SPEED MAX MOVING EWD OVER THE APPALACHIANS. THE 12Z RNK SOUNDING REVEALED THE POTENTIAL FOR MODERATE INSTABILITY WITH SURFACE TEMPERATURES IN THE 80S...AND SUFFICIENT BULK SHEAR TO MAINTAIN AN ORGANIZED STORM CLUSTER. THUS...THERE WILL BE THE POTENTIAL FOR THE ONGOING CONVECTION TO PERSIST FOR A FEW HOURS WITH THE THREAT FOR A FEW DAMAGING OUTFLOW GUSTS.

sections.title: OH VALLEY TO SAINT LAWRENCE VALLEY TODAY
sections.text: A BROAD AREA HAS SOME POTENTIAL FOR STRONG/DAMAGING DOWNBURST WINDS...YET INSTABILITY AND VERTICAL SHEAR ARE NOT PHASED PARTICULARLY WELL. STRONGER LOW-MIDLEVEL FLOW/SHEAR WILL RESIDE OVER THE SAINT LAWRENCE VALLEY/LOWER GREAT LAKES IN ASSOCIATION WITH THE MIDLEVEL TROUGH AND COLD FRONT MOVING EWD OVER ONTARIO/QUEBEC. THE STRONGER INSTABILITY WILL BE LOCATED FARTHER SW INTO THE OH VALLEY /W OF THE MORNING CONVECTION IMPACTING ERN KY AND WV/...BUT VERTICAL SHEAR WILL REMAIN WEAK THIS FAR SW. WILL OPT TO OUTLOOK A RELATIVELY LARGE 5% WIND AREA WITH THE EXPECTATION THAT ADDITIONAL OBSERVATIONAL DATA DURING THE DAY WILL HELP MORE ACCURATELY DELINEATE CORRIDORS WITH AN INCREASED SEVERE STORM THREAT THIS AFTERNOON...IF NEEDED. ..THOMPSON/GRAMS.. 07/17/2010

sections.title: UPPER MIDWEST/UPPER MS VALLEY
sections.text: SCATTERED SEVERE STORMS INCLUDING SUPERCELLS WILL CONTINUE TO DEVELOP ALONG/NORTH OF A RETREATING/BUT NOW CONVECTIVELY REINFORCED WARM FRONT FROM FAR SOUTHEAST ND SOUTHEASTWARD ACROSS CENTRAL MN TO CENTRAL WI. ADDITIONAL DEEP CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT SEEMS PROBABLE LATE THIS AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING FROM NEAR A SURFACE TRIPLE POINT ALONG THE SOUTHEAST ND/NORTHEAST SD BORDER VICINITY...SOUTHWESTWARD ALONG THE SOUTHEASTWARD ADVANCING COLD FRONT ACROSS EASTERN SD TO NEB. FOR ADDITIONAL DETAILS...SEE MESOSCALE DISCUSSION 1335. IN EITHER CASE...AN INITIAL SUPERCELLULAR MODE /WITH TORNADO AND LARGE HAIL POTENTIAL/ WILL YIELD TO UPSCALE/MCS-TYPE GROWTH THIS EVENING/TONIGHT...WITH AN APPRECIABLE/WIDESPREAD DAMAGING WIND THREAT INCREASING ACCORDINGLY ESPECIALLY ACROSS THE SOUTHERN HALF OF MN/NORTHERN IA/FAR WESTERN WI. CONSULT THE LATEST WATCHES/MESOSCALE DISCUSSIONS FOR THE MOST CONTEMPORARY GUIDANCE.

THIS FORCING IS PROGGED TO SLOWLY DEVELOP EASTWARD INTO PARTS OF WESTERN WISCONSIN THIS EVENING...BEFORE WEAKENING AROUND OR SHORTLY AFTER 06Z. SO FURTHER UPSCALE CONVECTIVE GROWTH AND INTENSIFICATION REMAINS A DISTINCT POSSIBILITY THIS EVENING IN THE PRESENCE OF MODERATE TO STRONG INSTABILITY. sections.title: OHIO VALLEY AND LOWER GREAT LAKES INTO THE NORTHEAST

COUPLED WITH SHEAR/ INSTABILITY COMBINATIONS SOMEWHAT ONLY MARGINALLY SUPPORTIVE OF ORGANIZED SEVERE STORMS...AND BECOMING MORE MARGINAL WITH THE LOSS OF DAYTIME HEATING...THE SEVERE POTENTIAL IS EXPECTED TO BECOME MORE ISOLATED AND GRADUALLY DIMINISH THROUGH THE 03-05Z TIME FRAME.

sections.title: SOUTHERN ARIZONA
sections.text: A SIGNIFICANT MESOSCALE CONVECTIVE SYSTEM CONTINUES TO PROPAGATE WESTWARD NEAR AND JUST SOUTH OF THE INTERNATIONAL BORDER...TOWARD THE NORTHERN GULF OF CALIFORNIA. ADDITIONAL STORM DEVELOPMENT IS POSSIBLE ALONG THE CONVECTIVELY GENERATED OUTFLOW BOUNDARY ACROSS SOUTHERN ARIZONA...AND OFF THE SOUTHEASTERN ARIZONA MOUNTAINS INTO THE LOWER DESERTS THIS EVENING. THOUGH ADDITIONAL DOWNBURSTS ARE POSSIBLE...THE SEVERE THREAT DOES NOT APPEAR LIKELY TO INCREASE FURTHER...AND IT PROBABLY WILL BEGIN TO WANE BY 02-04Z. ..KERR.. 07/18/2010
